Sega Games Co., Ltd. (2015-2020) }} '''Sega''' was originally founded in 1940 as "Standard Games" in Honolulu, Hawaii to provide amusement games to U.S. military facilities across Hawaii. The company was then moved to Tokyo, Japan by Raymond Lemaire and Richard Stewart as a means of distributing coin-operated games and was renamed to "Service Games" with Nihon Goraku Busan being its corporate name. In 1965, Nihon Goraku Busan purchased Rosen Enterprises and became "Sega Enterprises, Ltd." (an abbreviation for "'''Se'''rvice '''Ga'''mes"), its current identity. In 1969, the company was sold to Gulf+Western. Sega would soon become an immediate competitor to [[Nintendo]] right after they started manufacturing video game consoles (such as the Sega Master System, Genesis, etc.) and came up with their own iconic mascot Sonic the Hedgehog. In 1984, Nakayama and Rosen led a management buyout of the company with backing from CSK Corporation. On November 1, 2000, Sega Enterprises was renamed to Sega Corporation. In 2003, fellow video game and amusement company [[Sammy|Sammy Corporation]] purchased a controlling share in Sega. In 2004, Sammy completed its takeover of Sega, which led to the formation of Sega Sammy Holdings. In 2013, Sega purchased Index (which published games under the [[Atlus]] brand). In 2015, Sega Corporation was reorganized into Sega Group (which was legally named as Sega Holdings Co., Ltd.), a business segment of the Sega Sammy Group consolidating all of their entertainment businesses (including video games, amusement centers, animation studios and toys). Sega Games took over Sega's home consumer business while Sega Interactive was created to handle Sega's amusement businesses. In 2020, Sega Games and Sega Interactive were merged to form the second incarnation of Sega Corporation, while Sega Holdings became Sega Group Corporation. In 2024, Sega demerged and transferred their amusement machine business to Sega Toys which renamed itself to Sega Fave Corporation in the process. {{YouTube|id=kLVelULW1zE|id2=wbbxrDuv2Dw|id3=QzIrxRnKurw|description3= ''Sonic 3'' sales promotion version (starts at 2:53)|id4=ZjosyI5Rejo}} '''Visuals:''' On a white background, the blue Sega logo (consisting of the uppercase "'''SEGA'''", resembles a maze, composed of two dark blue stripes with a thin white line between them. The thin lines are remain at the center, except for the "A", looks like a triangle with a curved right leg to form a lower rib) is seen in the center. The animation varies depending on the game. Starting in the late 1990s, the "TM" symbol is replaced with a registered trademark symbol. '''Variants:''' * Sometimes, the logo appears on the title screen on numerous arcade games. * The 16-bit version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' and the unreleased arcade game ''SegaSonic Bros.'' have a light blue line moving around showing parts of the Sega logo, before it fades in. This is also seen on some prototypes of the 16-bit version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2''. * The Sega Genesis version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2'', and ''Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I'' have Sonic (the company's mascot) running around forming the logo. * On the Game Gear version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog'', Sonic forms the logo by jumping around. This can also be seen on Japanese commercials in the early 1990s, albeit in stop-motion. * On a sales promotion ad for ''Sonic 3'', the logo used in ''Sonic 2'' is used, but Sonic is replaced with a row of black lines. This was an artifact of the game being built off ''Sonic 2'', as a prototype version of the game was used here. * On some Game Gear games, the background is blue. * On ''Columns'' for the Sharp X1, the logo is shown shining. * On ''Sonic the Hedgehog 3'', ''Sonic and Knuckles'', ''Sonic 3 and Knuckles'' (including both the ''Sonic Origins'' and ''Sonic Origins Plus'' ports of the latter) and ''Sonic Mania'', the logo just fades in. ** However, there are different endings for all of those games: *** The ''Sonic and Knuckles'' variant ends with Sonic coming from the top, seguing into the game's title screen. * On ''Sonic Mania'', the logo is slightly brighter, and it is also enhanced as well. * Starting in 1994, the text "PRESENTED BY" is shown above the logo. * A light blue variation of the logo exists, which can be found on the Japanese and Asian versions of Sega titles. * On the original PC port of ''Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut'', the logo is on a white background and the view is also resized by the screen resolution (the bigger the resolution is, the smaller the logo gets) unless the fill modes under "UI Scaling" (in the graphics tab in SADX Mod Loader) was set to "Fit" or "Fill" with the loader installed. * On the international Nintendo DS versions of ''Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games'' and ''Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Winter Games'', "Published and developed by" is shown above the logo. * On the 2011 remake of ''Sonic CD'' for the PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PC, Android and iOS, the logo is on a dark blue background. This was replaced with the "Sega Forever" variant on the Android and iOS versions. * On ''Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode II'', both Sonic and Tails run around, as akin to ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2'' and ''Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I'', forming the Sega logo. * On ''Sonic Forces'', the logo is zoomed out further than usual. "Presented by" is not above the logo. * On ''Puyo Puyo Tetris 2'', "Presented by" is not above the logo. * On ''Sonic Shuffle'', "Presented by" is in the same font as the [[Dreamcast]] logo. * On ''Rhythm Tengoku'' for the [[Sega Naomi]], "Presented by" is in a different font, and is colored light blue. * On the official promotional ''Sonic The Hedgehog 3'' Genesis game, a compressed version of the print logo is used. * On promotional videos for Sonic games on Sega's 1996 website, the logo fades in, with the website URL placed below it. * Since 2018, the logo cuts in and then fades out. * On ''LEGO Dimensions Sonic the Hedgehog Level Pack'', with the level being titled "Sonic Dimensions", as part of the game's 2nd season, the LEGO Minifigure version of Sonic running the logo, similar to the Sega Genesis version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2'', and ''Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I'' variants. If you look closely, the blue LEGO bricks are shown when Sonic is running, as well as the lines from the SEGA logo when he runs to the left side. '''Trivia:''' The logo used in the 16-bit version of ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' and the unreleased arcade game ''SegaSonic Bros.'' was been parodied by The White House in a video promoting the arcade.gov website, which been later mentioned in numerous news reports. '''Technique:''' Usually a still graphic. The ''LEGO Dimensions Sonic the Hedgehog Level Pack'' is real-time CGI using [[TT Games]]'s Nu2 engine and is capped at 30fps. '''Audio:''' On many games, a choir singing "Se-ga!". This particular soundbite made its first appearance on Japanese advertisements for the SG-1000 (Sega's first console) in 1983. It can also be found on the ''[[Sonic Generations]]'' "20 Years of Sonic" compilation CD, as well as the "History of the 1st Stage - Original Soundtrack Blue and White Editions" as "SEGA Call" and the "GO SEGA - SEGA 60th Anniversary Album" as "[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3CBHgBkuQUs SEGA Sound Logo (SEGA Call)]". '''Audio Trivia:''' In ''Sonic Mania'', a variant of the classic Sega jingle, sung by attendents of the ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' 25th anniversary party, held at the House of Blues in San Diego, California on July 22, 2016, was planned for use, but it was scrapped for unknown reasons. '''Audio Variants:''' * On the Simon Wai prototype build of ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2'', the Sega jingle is noticeably higher pitched. * ''Sonic Mega Collection'', ''Sonic Gems Collection'', the 2011 remake of ''Sonic CD'' and ''Hell Yeah! Wrath of the Dead Rabbit'' use an enhanced version of the Sega jingle. Furthermore, SEGA AM-2 games on Xbox 360 and PS3 have the Sega jingle if holding B / Circle before the logo appears. In ''Virtua Fighter 5: Final Showdown'' / ''Virtua Fighter eSports'' if using the PS4, if the region is in North America or Europe, or PS5, as well as ''Virtua Fighter 5: R.E.V.O.'' (Original and ''World Stage''), it is switched to the A / Cross button (keyboard users will have to hold the Enter key instead), besides Nintendo Switch 2, which is reverted to the A button. * The ''Hatsune Miku: Project Diva'' series has Hatsune Miku (voice sampled by Saki Fujita) or her other Vocaloid friends yelling "Sega!". ** On the first three games in the series, Miku's voice sounds more synthesized. * ''K-On! Houkago Live!!'' has the lead character Yui Hirasawa (voiced by Aki Toyosaki) yelling "Sega!". Also in the game's files there are [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hDBsNY3tU-c unused voice lines] of Mio Akiyama (voiced by Yoko Hikasa), Ritsu Tainaka (voiced by Satomi Sato), Tsumugi Kotobuki (voiced by Minako Kotobuki), and Azusa Nakano (voiced by Ayana Taketatsu), yelling "Sega!" * ''Sonic Adventure'' for the Sega Dreamcast has one of the characters in the game say "Sega" in either Japanese or English. It also changes each time the game starts up. * Five of the games in the ''Puyo Puyo'' series, ''Puyo Puyo!! 20th Anniversary'', ''Puyo Puyo Quest!'', ''Puyo Puyo Tetris'', ''Puyo Puyo Chronicle'' and ''Puyo Puyo Puzzle Pop'', has one of the characters (in Japanese or English, starting from the PC version of ''Puyo Puyo Tetris'') in those games say "Sega", which changes each time the game starts up. ** The sound clips can also be played in the Sound Test menu, including ''Puyo Puyo Tetris 2'' (which is located on Voice Clip 46), which had the "Amazing Sega" sound by evala instead, as shown below. * Since 2018, a dramatic electronic synth with an echo effect from the 14th logo ("Amazing Sega") by evala is used. Some games also allow the player to skip the logo, which may cause the rest of the sound to play over the other logos, if possible. * The ''LEGO Dimensions Sonic the Hedgehog Level Pack'' had sound effects during the Sonic running part before the "Se-ga!" choir. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' * The logo first appeared on arcade games since 1981, starting with the 1981 Sega edition of ''Tactician''. * The logo can also be found on Master System games from 1987 to 1989, when running on a Japanese console, as well as the startups of the Master System II that featured the built-in games of ''Alex Kidd in Miracle World'' and ''[[osca:Sonic the Hedgehog (1991 video game)|Sonic the Hedgehog]]''. * The animated logo was first seen on ''Columns'' for the Sharp X1, but it's best known for its appearance on the ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' games, including the first three games (''[[osca:Sonic the Hedgehog (1991 video game)|Sonic the Hedgehog]]'', ''Sonic the Hedgehog 2'', ''Sonic the Hedgehog 3'', ''Sonic & Knuckles'' and ''Sonic 3 & Knuckles''), as well as several others. * It can also be found on most Sonic games, such as ''Sonic Adventure'', ''Sonic Adventure 2'', ''Sonic Heroes'', ''Sonic Advance'', and ''Sonic Forces'', as well as their latest game ''Sonic Frontiers''. * It can also be found seen on the cancelled ''Sonic DS'' demo. * This logo can also be found on a majority of arcade games produced by Sega, such as ''OutRun'', ''After Burner'', ''Daytona USA'' and the ''Initial D: Arcade Stage'' franchise. * The "Amazing Sega" sound variant can be heard on newer games that are released by the company after 2018, including rereleases of older games (such as ''Shenmue I&II'', ''Super Monkey Ball Banana Blitz HD'', the ''Maimai DX'' series and ''Banana Mania'', ''Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis'', and ''Sonic Colors: Ultimate'') and ports/remakes of games in the ''Like A Dragon'' franchise (formerly known as ''Yakuza''). ===2nd Logo ({{date|year=1983}}-{{date|year=1987}})=== [[File:Manufactured by Sega (1985) (Taken from Choplifter, SG-1000).png|center]] '''Visuals:''' On a black background is the Sega logo in blue that shimmers. '''Variant:''' Depending on the game, the colors may vary. '''Technique:''' 2D sprite animation. '''Audio:''' None, or the opening theme of the game. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on many SG-1000 games from the period, like ''Choplifter'', ''H.E.R.O.'', ''Bank Panic'' and ''Chack'n Pop'', among others. ===3rd Logo ({{date|year=1987}}-{{date|year=1989}})=== [[File:Manufactured by Sega in Japan (1988) (Taken from Bomber Raid, SEGAM3).png|300px|center]] '''Visuals:''' On a blue background is the Sega logo in black. The color then changes and flashes. '''Technique:''' 2D sprite animation. '''Audio:''' None, or the opening theme of the game. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on numerous Master System games when playing on a Japanese console, such as ''Dynamite Duke'', ''Bomber Raid'' and ''Gain Ground'.'' ===4th Logo ({{date|month=October|day=29|year=1988}}-2002, {{date|month=June|day=22|year=2017}}-April 4, 2019)=== Images= Sega (1989).jpeg Sega (1989).gif Sega (1993) (Taken from Aladdin, GEN).png Sega (1993) (Taken from RoboCop versus The Terminator, GEN).png Sega (1994) (Taken from NH Indy Car, GEN).png Sega (2017) (From - Comix Zone for mobile phones).png Sega (2017) iPad.png |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=5Y1J5E-Tv5k|id2=EVsV73Mwr8U}} '''Visuals:''' There is the Sega logo in its futuristic font (which is in blue and contains many white stripes around it) on a black background. On most games, the logo "shines" by having the color change in shades of blue. '''Variants:''' * Sometimes, the logo fades in and/or fades out. * In its early days since until 1991, the "®" symbol was used. Starting around late 1990, the "TM" symbol replaces the "®" symbol. * Sometimes, the logo lacks the trademark symbol. * On ''ATP Tour Championship Tennis'' and most game compilations for the Genesis, the logo appears via a turning on effect before shining as normal and disappears via a turning off effect. * A still version with no shining exists. * On games published or developed by [[Virgin Interactive|Virgin Interactive Entertainment]], the Sega logo shines quickly in a loop. * On mobile games under the Sega Forever series, the modern logo appears on-screen first, then it disintegrates into pixels that float away to the top right to reveal this logo, which shines after. '''Technique:''' 16-bit animation. '''Audio:''' None or the opening theme of the game. '''Audio Variants:''' * On ''The Story of Thor'' (known as ''Beyond Oasis'' in the U.S.), the SEGA choir plays after the logo shines. * On games produced by [[Infogrames]] (except for ''The Smurfs 2'') and ''Tinhead'', the SEGA choir plays in the form of a two-note jingle. * The Sega Forever variant has the Sonic ring loss sound effect, followed by the SEGA choir. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on most games for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis like ''Altered Beast''. Also appears on some games for the Sega Game Gear (and the Sega 32X attachment for the Genesis/Mega Drive). * Some of the only games not to use this logo were most Sega Master System games and every [[Electronic Arts]], [[Namco]], [[Codemasters]] and [[Tengen]] game for Sega Genesis (including [[EA Sports]] games as well), as well as the earliest [[Accolade]] licensed Genesis titles, including ''Bubsy in the Claws Encounters of the Furred Kind'', however, most copies of that game have this logo. * One EA Genesis game that contains the logo is ''Shaq Fu'', while ''Baku Baku Animal'', ''Bonkers Wax Up!'', ''Daffy Duck in Hollywood'', ''Double Dragon'', ''Lemmings'', ''Sonic Blast'', ''Streets of Rage'', ''Ultimate Soccer'' and ''Virtual Fighter Animation'' were the only Sega Master System games that contain the logo. * The logo can be also seen on EA Game Gear games. * It is generally left intact in most re-releases of Sega games of the time period like on Wii Virtual Console re-releases of Genesis games. * The logo also appears in the prototype of ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' on the Sega Genesis. ===5th Logo (March-September 1989)=== Image= [[File:Sega (1989).png|center|350px]] |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=60p0ciyN18s|id2=pTf9s7iTJn4|id3=_fUYD8KKV9M}} '''Visuals:''' On a black background is a modified version of the Sega logo (thinner than the usual one in white with Sega, a blue outline and with still shines on the "S" and "A"). "COMPUTER SOFTWARE" is beneath in the same color with "© 1989" in red and yellow below. "PROGRAM LOADING..." is on the bottom of the logo in the same color as the first two texts. '''Technique:''' A sprite graphic. '''Audio:''' None or the music of the game. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Only seen on MS-DOS ports of ''After Burner II'', ''Space Harrier'', and ''OutRun''. ===6th Logo (''Sonic CD'' prototypes custom variant) ({{date|month=December|day=4|year=1992}}-1993?)=== Image= [[File:Sonic cd - prototype sega logo.jpg|center|300px]] |-| Video= {{YouTube|id=RS2My1bsu6A}} '''Visuals:''' Essentially just a freeze-frame of the [[Sega Video]] logo. '''Technique:''' A CGI render. '''Audio:''' The "SEGA" jingle. '''AvailabiIity:''' Seen on early prototypes of ''Sonic The Hedgehog CD'', from prototypes v0.02 to v0.51. It was removed in later prototypes because it was included in the BIOS. ===7th Logo (''Ecco'' series custom variant) ({{date|month=August|day=25|year=1994}}-{{date|month=December|day=13|year=1996}})=== Images= Sega (1994) (ECCOː The Tides of Time).gif Sega (1995).jpeg |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=n0m7LdTfH88|id2=IIFnanvaepk}} '''Visuals:''' There is the Sega logo in a grayish-blue underwater background with bubbles floating toward the surface. '''Variant:''' On ''Ecco the Dolphin'' (PC), "'''PRESENTS a PC Conversion by'''" is below the logo. The background is also more realistic and is rippling. '''Technique:''' 16-bit animation. '''Audio:''' Underwater ambiance with a deep chord or the opening theme of the game. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on ''Ecco: The Tides of Time'' for the Mega Drive/Genesis, as well as ''Ecco the Dolphin'' for the PC. ===8th Logo (''Knuckles' Chaotix'' custom variant) ({{date|month=December|day=27|year=1994}}-June 1995)=== Images= SEGA (Knuckle's Chaotix).png Sega Logo (Chaotix prototype 1227).png |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=J8BLA1JBJRE|id2=V6J1R4WPTN0}} '''Visuals:''' On a purple space background, the Sega logo zooms into the screen, then goes back while "wiggling" like Jell-O. The logo then zooms into the screen again while going black. '''Trivia:''' The CGI-like render of Newtrogic High Zone was also used on Knuckles' Chaotix's Japanese box art, on the back cover. '''Technique:''' 32-bit animation. '''Prototype Variant:''' On prototype 1227-0119 of the game, the background is a CGI-like rendering of Newtrogic High Zone. '''Audio:''' None, although on the prototypes, there are two different sound variations: * Prototype 0202 has a long synth-like sound. * Prototype 0208-0216 had a redone version of the sound, sounding like a synth rendition of the SEGA chant, but suspiciously like the NBC chimes. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Only seen on ''Knuckles' Chaotix'' for the 32X add-on. ===9th Logo (''Sonic 3D Blast'' custom variant) ({{date|month=November|day=8|day2=14|year=1996}})=== Image= Sega (1996) (Sonic 3D Blast).gif |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=avciU-0PbB8|id2=Gkx8ocGArHI}} '''Visuals:''' On a navy blue background, several wavy, light blue lines form the Sega logo letter by letter. When the logo finishes forming, the background color fades to white, and the logo changes to its standard blue color, with a trademark symbol ("™") next to the "A". Then, the background cycles through shades of blue as each of the letters in the logo fly past the camera, except for the "A", which zooms directly into the camera as the screen fades to black. '''Variant:''' On prototypes 73-819, the Sega logo breaks like glass instead of flying away letter by letter. '''Technique:''' 16-bit animation. '''Audio:''' A man screaming "SEGA!" (which was also used in North American Sega commercials of the time) when the logo finishes forming, followed by a set of descending synth noises from ''Sonic the Hedgehog 3'', ''Sonic & Knuckles'' and ''Sonic 3 & Knuckles'' when the letters fly out. * The "SEGA" chant is used in the prototypes. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Only seen on the Mega Drive/Genesis versions of ''Sonic 3D Blast'' (known in Europe as ''Sonic 3D: Flickies' Island''). The prototype version is seen on prototypes 73-819 of the game. ===10th Logo (''Sakura Wars'' / ''Sakura Taisen'' custom variant) ({{date|month=February|day=24|month2=September|day2=21|year=2000}})=== Images= Sega (Sakura Project 2000 variant, 2001).jpeg Sega (2000) (Sakura Project 2000 variant).jpeg |-| Videos= {{YouTube|id=ckyBv7EET-Y|id2=YwZvpQcjG1w}} '''Visuals:''' On a black background, there are some cherry blossom petals that float up into the sky with the Sega logo fading in, which briefly turns pink for a moment before it transitions to its blue color. '''Trivia:''' This variant was created as part of "SAKURA PROJECT 2000". '''Variants:''' * On ''Ogami Ichirou Funtouki'', the "Presented by" text is shown seconds after the Sega logo is formed, but in a different font. * On the Dreamcast ports of ''Sakura Wars'' / ''Sakura Taisen'' and ''Sakura Wars 2: Thou Shall Not Die'' / ''Sakura Taisen 2: Kimi, Shinitamou koto Nakare'' the final portion of the logo is reanimated to add the "Presented by" text atop the Sega logo. '''Technique:''' CGI animation. '''Audio:''' A gentle electronic theme. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Only seen on ''Sakura Wars'' / ''Sakura Taisen'' related games for Dreamcast, such as ''Ogami Ichirou Funtouki'' and ports of ''Sakura Wars'' / ''Sakura Taisen'' and ''Sakura Wars 2'' / ''Sakura Taisen 2'' for said system, as well as ''Sakura Wars'' / ''Sakura Taisen'' related material released during that period, such as VHS, DVD, and LaserDisc releases of the 2000 anime. ===11th Logo (''Yakuza'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' custom variant) ({{date|month=December|day=8|year=2005}}-{{date|month=September|day=15|year=2006}})=== {{YouTube|id=o39ZwegVNVw}} '''Visuals:''' There is a grid containing rapidly changing letters, numbers, symbols and the letters of the Sega logo. Then, the words "WHAT DO YOU WANT?" appear. Shortly after that, the screen moves horizontally when the word "DREAM" appear. Then, the screen moves vertically again as the word "EXCITEMENT?" appears and after that the word "TECHNOLOGY?" appears. Shortly after that, the arrows appear moving until the word "AND" appears. The word later turns upside down while a heart is shown. Then, the words "I GIVE IT" appear. After that, the words "I AM" appear before panning down to reveal the word "SEGA" in cursive-style lettering. The grid disappears while the actual Sega logo appears on the bottom with the words "Presented by" being located on the left of the logo. '''Technique:''' A mix of CGI and 128-bit animation. '''Audio:''' An upbeat electronic theme, which was listed as the first track of the ''Yakuza'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' soundtrack (the first disc of the ''Yakuza'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' and ''Yakuza 2'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku 2'' soundtracks), entitled "Service Games 2005", composed by Hidenori Shoji. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on ''Yakuza'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' for the PlayStation 2. ===12th Logo ({{date|month=November|day=7|year=2006}}-{{date|month=October|day=12|year=2017}})=== Images= SEGA (2006) (early variant).jpeg Presented by Sega (2006) 16ː9.png Presented by Sega (2006) 16ː9 (Europe).png Presented by Sega (2006) 4ː3 Open Matte (Europe).png Sega (Alpha Protocol).png Sega (Sonic Forces, in-credit).png Presented by Sega (2006) 4ː3 Open Matte.png Sega (2006).jpeg |-| Video= {{YouTube|id=Oanlky-T0Bg}} '''Visuals:''' On a black background, several trails of different colored lights move across the screen at a rapid pace, which come together and form the Sega logo. '''Variants:''' * A light blue variation also exists, which can be found on Japanese and Asian versions of Sega titles. However, this variant had a much brighter Sega logo than their print logo in Asia. * On ''Alpha Protocol'', a red streak runs through the formed logo, coloring it golden. The classic SEGA choir can also be heard. * On ''The Conduit'' is several circles adjusting around the pyramid with the Eye of Providence above. They match and form "SEGA", which shines and reveals as a regular logo. The whoosh and the announcer are heard as well. * On ''Iron Man 2'' for the PSP, a blue spot lights on and creates blocks which form the computerized Sega logo. * An early variation of the logo exists, where the text "Presented by" appears on top of the logo. * A still variant exists, but in the remake of ''Castle of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse'', the whoosh and the announcer is heard as well. ** Pressing the A / Cross (Circle in Japan and Asia besides PS5) / Enter (key) (Xbox/Nintendo consoles, PlayStation, and PC (via keyboard) respectively) button the animated version may apparently cause this. * An in-credit version also exists. '''Technique:''' CGI. '''Audio:''' A synth whooshing while the logo forms, followed by a male announcer saying "Sega". '''Audio Variants:''' * In the North American, European and Australian versions of ''Samba De Amigo'' for the Wii, a male announcer says the company name, then chuckles after the logo forms, just like in the original games, as well as the Japanese version, but without saying "Presented by" or "Produced by" before that. * In ''Bleach: Versus Crusade'', Ichigo Kurosaki (voiced by Masakazu Morita) yells the company name after the logo forms. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' * Used along with the 4th logo, mainly for external publishing, besides some games in Japan. * Seen on several games from 2006 until 2017, such as Sonic games like ''Sonic the Hedgehog'' (2006), ''Sonic and the Secret Rings'', ''Sonic Riders: Zero Gravity'', ''Sonic Unleashed'', ''Sonic and the Black Knight'', ''Sonic Colors'', ''Sonic Free Riders'', ''Sonic Generations'', ''Sonic Lost World'', and ''Sonic Boom: Rise of Lyric'', as well as other games including ''The Incredible Hulk'', ''Alpha Protocol'', ''The Club'', ''Iron Man'', ''Valkyria Chronicles'' and its sequel, ''Super Monkey Ball: Step & Roll'', ''The House of Dead 4'', the Xbox 360, PS3 and PC versions of ''NiGHTS... into Dreams'' and ''Sega Genesis/Mega Drive Collection''. ===13th Logo (''Yakuza 2'' / Ryū ga Gotoku 2 custom variant) ({{date|month=December|day=7|year=2006}}-{{date|month=September|day=19|year=2008}})=== {{YouTube|id=oD2ilMm_-lI}} '''Visuals:''' On a white background, an offscreen brush writes the word "SEGA" in Japanese calligraphy-style lettering. After the letters are written, a red stamp is placed on the bottom of the A (representing New Entertainment (now Sega CS1, then later [[Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio]]), the division that houses the team behind the ''Yakuza'' / ''Like a Dragon'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' games). Then, the background turns into a flag as it flies to the right. Then, the Sega logo is shown in the same format as how it was shown in the first ''Yakuza'' game. '''Technique:''' CGI animation. '''Audio:''' Rock music, which was listed as the first track of the ''Yakuza 2'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku 2'' soundtrack (the second disc of the ''Yakuza'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku'' and ''Yakuza 2'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku 2'' soundtracks), entitled "Service Games 2006", composed by Hidenori Shoji. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on ''Yakuza 2'' / ''Ryū ga Gotoku 2'' for the PlayStation 2. ===14th Logo (Amazing Sega) ({{date|month=May|day=18|year=2017}}-)=== Image= [[File:AmazingSega2017.jpeg|center|350px]] |-| Video= {{YouTube|id=5LilsZkQkdo}} '''Visuals:''' There is a close zoom-in of a person's blue eye at an angle in front of a white background. The North American and European Sega logo can be seen reflected inside of the eye, upon which the logo rotates to the right. As the Sega logo gradually comes to a stop, the eye widens in size and the pupil grows larger. In the static version, used for its games, the static Sega logo appears (see the 1st logo). '''Trivia:''' This logo was introduced as part of a new "''Amazing Sega''" corporate identity introduced by the company. The concept for this identity (and by extension, the logo) is based on studies based on the eye being the first part of the body to respond to an "amazing" experience. However, a static Sega logo is used in games instead. The concept video can be shown [https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=y50nAoA5KwY here] with English subtitles and it doesn't have Tashihiro Nagoshi saying "Amazing Sega" at the end of the video. Note that the Japanese version of the video, as well as the making of the video, which has been posted on Sega's Japanese YouTube channel, have been marked as private. '''Technique:''' Seems to be a mix of live-action and CGI effects. A digital graphic for the static version. This is planned and produced by SEGA in collaboration with Quaras, robot and WOW. '''Audio:''' A rising droning sound, promptly followed by a dramatic electronic synth with an echo effect. This is designed by evala. '''Audio Variant:''' For the games, just the synth is heard, but with a somewhat different echo, similar to the start of each trailer and commercial. '''Audio Trivia:''' The sound can also be found in the "GO SEGA - SEGA 60th Anniversary Album", in both the "[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=scGxVHDIoMw Top]" and "[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwgMCSrbC20 Last]" versions. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' This logo is seen in future Sega games going forward at the end of each trailer and commercial since 2017, replacing the previous logo. * It was first seen on the ''Sonic Forces'' story trailer. ===15th Logo (Empower the Gamers) ({{date|month=June|day=4|year=2024}})=== {{youtube|id=I2shxkrPOpY}} '''Visuals:''' On a light blue background, there is the Sega logo forming via two different angles, alongside the words "We" and "Are" superimposed with glitchy-like rectangles. After that, the Sega logo forms itself and the background transitions to white. The Sega logo splits into two: the light blue one representing Sega Corporation (including Sega Publishing Korea, Sega Singapore and Sega Taiwan) and the dark blue one representing Sega West (Sega of America and Sega Europe). Both logos briefly zoom out before fading to white. '''Technique:''' A mix of CGI and digital traditional animation. '''Audio:''' An electronic theme mixed with violin notes. '''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' Seen on the 2024 "Sega Mission Image Video".
